Where it started

A notepad at the table, then retype it all

It began as a way to keep track of selections for the contractors I work with.

Every selection was written down once, then typed again for the follow-up email, then figured again for the materials.

Notepad pageMaster bath: 12×24 Calacatta, 1/8" joint, warm gray grout. Hall: 7×48 River Oak. "Wants a sample."
The follow-up emailAll of it typed out again so the contractor has it in writing.Subject: Re: selections — Miller main floor
Grout & mortar, by handCoverage chart and a calculator, once per size, once per area.231 ÷ 146.7 = 1.57 → 2 bags
Price sheet binderFind the SKU, find the carton size, write the price down, then type it again.
Sticky note"Did anyone order the Kessel sample?"
Shower parts listPan, curb, panels, sealant, fasteners, worked out line by line from the vendor catalog.

Start with the customer

Open the customer, and the job is there

  • Search by name, phone or address, grouped by salesperson.
  • Every project under the customer, with its number, its selections and its samples.
  • Contact details entered once, used by every print and email.
  • Quick Price for a walk-in: a draft with no customer yet that promotes when they sign.

Sample directory. Selecting a customer lists their projects below.

Price sheets, attached

Most of what we sell, one search

  • Search from the row. Type a SKU or a name in the selection and the price, carton and coverage fill in. Typos and trade names still find it.
  • Nothing written down. No copying from a binder at the table or the computer. The pricing is ready to go.
  • Import once. Drop the vendor sheet, map the columns. Excel and text PDFs both work.
  • Re-import safely. The review shows what is new, changed and retiring before it lands. A stale sheet warns on the job.

Selections and extras

The grout color travels with the tile

  • Extras attach to the selection. Grout, its color and joint, mortar, caulk and trims sit under the tile they belong to.
  • An easy dropdown. Grout, mortar and trims are picked from a short list, not typed.
  • Set up for anything. Add a category for trowels, sealer or whatever else we sell with the job.
  • It prints and orders that way too. The grout puck rides the tile line and the extras total below it.

On screen: the grout and mortar line under the tile.

On paper: grout and caulk in the Extras band.

Our own categories, coverage or per-row.

If someone overrides a quantity

Sq ft now calculates to 3  ·  this row is set to 2 Use 3

An override is a decision, so it stays. When the footage moves, the row says what it would calculate now, one click to take it.

Configurators

Choose a pan, the shower builds itself

  • wedi shower systemsPick a pan and everything for a basic shower is put together. Modify it from there.
  • SchluterThe same build with the KERDI system, priced from the registry.
  • Sheoga hardwoodCustom flooring without building it by hand. Species, width, grade and finish, priced live.
  • Compare wedi and SchluterOne room, both systems, line by line. Lands as Option A and B on the job.

Add to product lines, print, or copy for order entry from any of them.

Pricing

Tiers, freight, waste and options

  • Pricing tiers. Retail, Builder, Employee, Sale or a custom percent, for the whole quote at once.
  • Freight figures itself. Each vendor's rate program, minimums and pallet thresholds, charged once per order.
  • Waste figures itself. One rate for tile, one for other flooring, applied before the order quantity.
  • Options on one quote. Tag an area Option A, B and so on. Shared rooms stay shared, and the print shows every option's total.

The job header: price level, waste and freight in one bar.

Freight on the print, figured per vendor program.

Two options, two totals, one sheet.

Saved as you go

When the conversation ends, the job is done

  • Every pick saves itself. Looking at products with the customer builds the job.
  • No write-up afterwards. The quote, the materials and the samples list already exist.
  • Any device. Desk, tablet or phone on the showroom floor, cloud synced.
  • The whole team sees it. Every customer and project is shared.

Same job, on a phone.

Samples

Everyone can see what was requested

  • Request from the line. Right-click a selection, request a sample.
  • Visible to the team. The customer list shows how many are to order and how many are ordered.
  • One email per vendor. Grouped, addressed to the customer, ready to send.
  • Mark all ordered. One click, and the status is shared.

The Samples column on the customer list.

Formatted every way it is needed

Email for samples

  • Lines keyed for order entry, cartons as cartons, mouldings with their length.
